## The condensate borrow {#sec-ch08-borrow}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- A negative condensate is repaired by borrowing the deficit from the parent vapour in the same cell.
- Switch: part of the conserved limiter; applies to clouds that carry parent-vapour metadata.
- Exactly conservative in mass, energy and elements, unlike clamping the condensate to zero.
- Per-cell, so a ghost copy receives the identical repair and ranks stay in step.
- A cell whose vapour cannot cover the deficit goes vapour-negative and is left to the column repair.
:::

This is the one repair in the chapter that is conservative, and it is worth separating from the floors
it sits among for exactly that reason. The outline asks for it as its own scheme and the distinction
earns the space.

### Derivation

A negative condensate does not mean mass is missing. It means the tracer flux over-drained the cell and
the mass is in a neighbour. Clamping it to zero invents that mass, one way, every time.

The alternative the code takes is to move mass between rows of the same cell: take the deficit out of
the parent vapour and set the condensate to exactly zero. Total mass in the cell is unchanged, and so
are the elements, because vapour and its condensate are the same substance in different phases.

`[C3]` measures the difference rather than asserting it. Over two thousand cells with a negative
condensate, clamping to zero adds $3.770\times10^{-2}$ of mass, while the borrow changes the total by
exactly $0$. The code comment at `parentless` ([`equation_of_state.cpp:242-252`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L242-L252)) records the motivation from a
measurement: the clamp was responsible for $102\%$ of the total-mass drift in silicate cloud runs, which
is a number from a run that this chapter cites rather than reproduces.

### Numerical method

The repair is `parent_slot` ([`equation_of_state.cpp:252-269`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L252-L269)). For each cloud row with parent metadata, the
deficit is the negative part at `clamp_max` ([`equation_of_state.cpp:264`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L264)), it is added to each parent vapour
in proportion to its mass fraction at [`equation_of_state.cpp:265-267`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/eos/equation_of_state.cpp#L265-L267), and the condensate is
then set to exactly zero.

Two conditions are worth noting. A cloud not produced by nucleation has no parent metadata and is
skipped, flagged for the column repair of @sec-ch08-fixvapor instead. And the repair is purely local, so
a ghost cell that holds a copy of the same state receives the identical repair without any
communication, which is what keeps ranks consistent.

No ctest isolates the borrow.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- A cell whose vapour cannot cover the deficit goes vapour-negative. The borrow does not fail there; it
  hands the problem to the column repair, which may itself fail.
:::

1. **The phase shift is not free.** The repair moves mass between phases, which the code comment puts at
   about one per cent of the local value and expects the saturation adjustment to re-equilibrate within
   the same cycle. That expectation is a hypothesis recorded in the code; no test in the repository
   measures the residual phase error after the adjustment.
2. **Parentless clouds.** Clouds without nucleation metadata get no borrow at all, and the chapter
   cannot say how common that case is in practice.
